strings.d1.s0.name: Icherisheher Eski Şehir
strings.d1.s0.tips: A walled 12th-century city and UNESCO site: narrow lanes, the setting of the film Brilliant Hand, carpet shops.
strings.d1.s1.name: Maiden Tower
strings.d1.s1.tips: A mysterious 8-storey tower (Zoroastrian?); from the top you see the Caspian and the Flame Towers.
strings.d1.s2.name: Palace of the Shirvanshahs
strings.d1.s2.tips: The 15th-century Shirvanshahs' palace: mausoleum, divan hall, bathhouse.
strings.d1.s3.name: Firuze Restaurant Old City
strings.d1.s3.tips: Azerbaijani cuisine: kutab (thin stuffed flatbread), piti, saj.
strings.d1.s4.name: Baku Boulevard
strings.d1.s4.tips: A 3.7 km promenade (1909) on the Caspian shore: Ferris wheel, gondola rides in Little Venice. After 20:00 take the funicular up to Highland Park and watch the Flame Towers light show.
strings.d1.b0.name: Sehirli Tendir
strings.d1.b0.tips: Tandir bread and kutab; an Old City street.
strings.d1.b1.name: Museum of Miniature Books
strings.d1.b1.tips: Guinness record-holding miniature books; free, an alternative to the palace.
strings.d2.theme: Heydar Aliyev and the Carpet Museum
strings.d2.s0.name: Heydar Aliyev Center
strings.d2.s0.tips: Zaha Hadid's undulating white masterpiece; classic car exhibition, photographing the exterior is free.
strings.d2.s1.name: Azerbaijan Carpet Museum
strings.d2.s1.tips: A building shaped like a rolled carpet; on the Boulevard, with a weaving demonstration.
strings.d2.s2.name: Nargiz Restaurant Bulvar
strings.d2.s2.tips: Azerbaijani cuisine with Caspian views; dolma and kebab.
strings.d2.s3.name: Nizami Street Torgovaya
strings.d2.s3.tips: A pedestrian shopping street lined with 19th-century oil baron mansions.
strings.d2.s4.name: Baku Crystal Hall and Flag Square Walk
strings.d2.s4.tips: The Eurovision 2012 arena; sunset at the end of the Boulevard.
strings.d2.b0.name: Museum of Modern Art Baku
strings.d2.b0.tips: Azerbaijani modern art; an alternative to the carpet museum.
strings.d2.b1.name: Paul's Bakery Fountains Square
strings.d2.b1.tips: Coffee and pastries on the square.
strings.d3.s0.name: Gobustan Rock Art
strings.d3.s0.tips: 60 km south (tour about 40 AZN, or a taxi); more than 6,000 rock carvings up to 10,000 years old, UNESCO site, museum.
strings.d3.s1.name: Gobustan Mud Volcanoes
strings.d3.s1.tips: Azerbaijan has half of the world's mud volcanoes: bubbling cold mud cones, reached by old Lada.
strings.d3.s2.name: Bibi-Heybat Mosque
strings.d3.s2.tips: On the Caspian shore, a mosque destroyed by the Soviets and later rebuilt; set among oil pumps.
strings.d3.s3.name: Qobustan Yolu Balık Lokantası
strings.d3.s3.tips: Caspian fish (kutum) and levengi (stuffed fish or chicken); on the way.
strings.d3.s4.name: Yanar Dag
strings.d3.s4.tips: A gas-fuelled hillside that has burned continuously for 60 years, rooted in Zoroastrian tradition; striking in the dark, 25 km north.
strings.d3.b0.name: Ateshgah Fire Temple
strings.d3.b0.tips: The Surakhani Zoroastrian-Hindu fire temple; in the same direction as Yanar Dag, as a substitute or an addition.
strings.d3.b1.name: Qala Köy Restoranı
strings.d3.b1.tips: Tandir and saj dishes next to the ethnographic village; instead of a roadside restaurant.
strings.d4.s0.name: Ateshgah of Baku
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Surakhani fire temple (17th-century Hindu-Zoroastrian): natural gas flame, pilgrims' cells.
strings.d4.s1.name: Qala Archaeological Ethnographic Complex
strings.d4.s1.tips: An open-air museum village on the Absheron peninsula: fortress, tandir, camels.
strings.d4.s2.name: Mardakan Castle and Town
strings.d4.s2.tips: A 14th-century castle and arboretum; Yesenin's house.
strings.d4.s3.name: Mardakan Balık Tavernası
strings.d4.s3.tips: Grilled fish in a seaside town.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bilgah Beach Hazar
strings.d4.s4.tips: Swimming in the Caspian (low salinity); Bilgah beach, in summer.
strings.d4.b0.name: Amburan Beach Club
strings.d4.b0.tips: A beach club with sunloungers; Bilgah.
strings.d4.b1.name: Gala Köyü Çayhanesi
strings.d4.b1.tips: Tea in pear-shaped glasses with jam; in the village.
strings.d5.s0.name: Sheki Khan's Palace
strings.d5.s0.tips: 4 hours from Baku (early tour or car; ideally stay overnight); a 1762 palace with shebeke stained glass, UNESCO site, built without nails.
strings.d5.s1.name: Sheki Caravanserai
strings.d5.s1.tips: An 18th-century caravanserai hotel; courtyard and vaulted halls.
strings.d5.s2.name: Şeki Piti Öğle Gagarin
strings.d5.s2.tips: Sheki's piti soup served in a clay pot (ritual: eat the broth with bread first, then mash the meat); Sheki halva.
strings.d5.s3.name: Kish Albanian Church
strings.d5.s3.tips: A Caucasian Albanian church (legend dates it to the 1st century); Thor Heyerdahl's theory; village setting.
strings.d5.s4.name: Sheki Halva Workshop
strings.d5.s4.tips: Sheki halva as a souvenir; on the way back (Baku 20:00).
strings.d5.b0.name: Gabala Tufandag Cable Car
strings.d5.b0.tips: A Caucasus mountain cable car and Lake Nohur; closer than Sheki (3 hours), as an alternative.
strings.d5.b1.name: Lahic Village Tea House
strings.d5.b1.tips: Tea and kebab in a cobbled coppersmith village; an alternative on the road to Sheki.
strings.d6.s0.name: Taza Bazaar
strings.d6.s0.tips: A local market: pomegranates, saffron, sumac, cheese tasting, dried fruit.
strings.d6.s1.name: Baku Funicular and Martyrs' Lane by Day
strings.d6.s1.tips: Martyrs' Lane and the Eternal Flame by day; the Turkish Martyrs' Mosque.
strings.d6.s2.name: Sumakh Restaurant
strings.d6.s2.tips: A stylish Azerbaijani restaurant: saj and kutab, in Khagani Street.
strings.d6.s3.name: Baku Sea Boat Tour
strings.d6.s3.tips: A 1-hour Caspian boat tour from the Boulevard; the skyline.
strings.d6.s4.name: Nizami Cinema and Passage Cafes in the Evening
strings.d6.s4.tips: Seaside Park and Torgovaya tea houses; shisha.
strings.d6.b0.name: Stone Chronicle Museum
strings.d6.b0.tips: A museum of stone inscriptions; on the Boulevard.
strings.d6.b1.name: Çay Bağı 145 Eski Şehir
strings.d6.b1.tips: Tea and jam in the Old City; the Azerbaijani tea tradition.
strings.d7.theme: Boulevard morning and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Boulevard Morning Walk Little Venice
strings.d7.s1.name: Mugham Center
strings.d7.s1.tips: A building shaped like a tar (a long-necked lute); on the Boulevard, seen from outside.
strings.d7.s2.name: Qaynana Restaurant Breakfast
strings.d7.s2.tips: Azerbaijani breakfast: clotted cream, honey, tandir bread, kuymak (cornmeal and cheese); next to Fountains Square.
strings.d7.s3.name: Baku Airport Bus H1
strings.d7.s3.tips: From 28 May the H1 bus, 40 minutes (BakiKart); farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Ali and Nino Bookshop Cafe
strings.d7.b0.tips: Breakfast in a bookshop cafe; the city of the novel.
strings.d7.b1.name: Government House
strings.d7.b1.tips: A huge Stalin-era building on Azadliq Square; seen from outside.
strings.note0: BakiKart (metro/bus 0.50 AZN); Bolt taxis are cheap. The H1 bus runs to the airport. For Gobustan and Sheki, take a tour or hire a car.
strings.note1: Summer brings 30-35°C and the Baku wind (Khazri); Caspian beach at Bilgah, the Boulevard in the evening; the F1 Grand Prix is held in June (the city centre closes).
strings.note2: Turkish citizens get 30 days visa-free (with ID card since 2025); 1 manat ≈ 0.6 USD; kutab 2 AZN, piti 8, restaurant meals 20-30, museums 5-15; tip 10%.
strings.note3: The Flame Towers light up after 21:00; Yanar Dag is best in the evening; Heydar Aliyev Center is closed on Mondays.
strings.note4: Piti, kutab, plov (shah plov), dolma, levengi, Sheki halva, pomegranate juice, pear-shaped glass tea with jam.
strings.note5: Turkish is understood (Azerbaijani Turkish); Russian is widespread. An oil city: pumps at Bibi-Heybat.
